 South America Magnitude 6.8 quake in Peru’s Andean region sends Lima residents onto streets
 The quake, which was felt in the capital Lima, struck in the Andean region of Junin at a depth of 129 km, according to Peru‘s geophysics institute. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck central Peru on Friday. Luis Robayo / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 20, 2026, 7:39 PM EST  /  Updated   Nov. 20, 2026, 9:54 PM EST / Source : Reuters By Reuters LIMA, Peru — A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, the German Research Centre for Geosciences said, sending some in the capital Lima into the streets, though there were no immediate reports of casualties or significant damage.
 The quake, which was felt in the capital Lima, struck in the Andean region of Junin at a depth of 129 km, according to Peru‘s Geophysical Institute.
 In Lima, residents evacuated their homes, and television footage showed lawmakers leaving Congress.

 “So far, no damage has been reported. This is the first time an earthquake of this magnitude has been felt in this area,” he said.

 Slide 1 of 1 Junin is home to several midsize mining operations as well as the Chinalco-owned Toromocho mine, one of Peru‘s largest copper mines. Peru is the world’s third-largest copper producer, and mining is a key driver of the economy.
 The US Tsunami Warning System said there was no tsunami threat following the earthquake.
 Peru lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire, a seismically active zone where tectonic plate movements frequently trigger quakes.
